svg.title: hybrid-minimax
svg.desc: MiniMax layouts from config.json. Text-01 (Jan 2025) and M1 (Jun 2025): 80 layers, 70 lightning-attention plus 10 softmax, KV 40 KiB per token. M2 (Oct 2025): 62 full GQA layers, 248 KiB. M3 (2026): 3 dense plus 57 sparse MSA layers, 120 KiB retained per token, each query reads 16 blocks of 128 tokens plus a local block. The M2 blog gives four reasons for leaving the hybrid: multi-hop reasoning deficits that appeared only at scale, costly evaluation and late-surfacing precision problems, immature infrastructure (memory-bound kernels, low-precision state, prefix caching, speculative decoding), and a sliding-window hybrid that degraded with context length.

text.font-family: STIX Two Math,Cambria Math,Times New Roman,serif

svg.text: Why M2 went back to full attention (MiniMax blog, 2025-10-30)
Multi-hop reasoning deficits showed only at scale; old benchmarks missed them.
Hard tasks need huge runs for a signal; precision bugs surfaced in M1 RL.
Memory-bound kernels; low-precision state; prefix caching; speculative decoding.
Continued pretraining into an SWA hybrid degraded as context grew.
Same blog: the theoretical compute/memory crossover lies at a few thousand tokens.
